claim: Scheduled scaling and scaling policies can be used together on one group: after a scheduled action runs, the scaling policy keeps deciding whether to scale further, while capacity must stay within the minimum and maximum set by the scheduled action.
question: Can a scheduled action and a target tracking policy work on the same Auto Scaling group, and how do they interact?

values.display: use scheduled scaling and scaling policies together
must fall within the minimum and maximum capacity

evidence.quote: You can use scheduled scaling and scaling policies together to get the benefits of both approaches to scaling.
After a scheduled scaling action runs, the scaling policy can continue to make decisions about whether to further scale capacity.
While your application scales to match demand, current capacity must fall within the minimum and maximum capacity that was set by your scheduled action.

note: Demand d76 (Callvale: target tracking plus a scheduled action before the morning peak).

claim: Recurring scheduled actions use UTC by default; you can set a local IANA time zone, and a location-based time zone adjusts automatically for Daylight Saving Time.
question: Which time zone does a recurring scheduled action use by default, and does it adjust for Daylight Saving Time?

values.display: the action automatically adjusts for DST

evidence.quote: By default, the recurring schedules that you set are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
When you specify a time zone that observes Daylight Saving Time (DST), the action automatically adjusts for DST.

note: Demand d76 (08:45 local time scheduled action).

claim: The default instance warmup is not enabled by default; AWS strongly recommends enabling and configuring it to optimize target tracking and step scaling policies.
question: Is the default instance warmup enabled by default, and what does AWS recommend?

values.display: It is not enabled or configured by default.
strongly recommend that you enable and configure

evidence.quote: To optimize the performance of your target tracking and step scaling policies, we strongly recommend that you enable and configure the default instance warmup.
It is not enabled or configured by default.

claim: The default instance warmup is how long an instance waits after reaching InService before its usage data counts in the aggregated metrics, so new instances with temporarily high startup usage do not distort dynamic scaling.
question: What does the default instance warmup control?

values.display: waits before contributing usage data to the aggregated metrics

evidence.quote: You can specify how long after an instance reaches the `InService` state it waits before contributing usage data to the aggregated metrics.

This keeps dynamic scaling from being affected by metrics for individual instances that aren't yet handling application traffic and that might be experiencing temporarily high usage of compute resources.

note: Demand d76: Callvale's 4-minute warmup maps to this setting.

claim: Without a default instance warmup, instance refresh uses the health check grace period as its warmup, target tracking and step scaling policies use the default cooldown value, and predictive scaling policies have no default warmup.
question: What warmup do instance refresh, target tracking and predictive scaling use when no default instance warmup is set?

values.display: uses the health check grace period as the default warmup time
value set for the default cooldown
they have no default warmup time

evidence.quote: For example, if you don't set a default instance warmup, the instance refresh feature uses the health check grace period as the default warmup time.
If you have any target tracking and step scaling policies, they use the value set for the default cooldown as the default warmup time.
If you have any predictive scaling policies, they have no default warmup time.

note: Demand d76. Display 'uses the health check grace period as the default warmup time' is 10 words; registrar may cut to 'health check grace period'.

claim: While new instances are warming up, dynamic scaling blocks scale-in activities until they finish warming up, and warming-up instances count as group capacity when it decides how many instances to add.
question: How does dynamic scaling treat instances that are still warming up?

values.display: blocks the scale in activities for dynamic scaling

evidence.quote: This blocks the scale in activities for dynamic scaling until the new instances finish warming up.
While scaling out, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling considers instances that are warming up as part of the capacity of the group when deciding how many instances to add to the group.
